Implementation Plan

Plan for issue #6532 / #6809: require a passing CI `lint` check-run before a stable release, and add a `STABLE_RELEASE_ENABLED` switch that is off by default

Planning ref: `git rev-parse HEAD` = 11f5f2c731355e086bd4f9731d00673955c768c7, symbolic branch `main`. The issue has no integration-branch metadata, so there is no mismatch.

Scope-mode: Hold Scope
Reuse-audit: extends release job "Record the tested commit" / "Verify CI passed" pattern in .github/workflows/mark-stable.yml and .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml (gh_retry from scripts/gh_helpers.sh)
Scope-mode justification: The unblock verdict sets the scope to exactly five paths: the two release workflows, one test file, `README.md` and one changelog fragment. Nothing is added beyond that. The test goes into the existing `tests/test_mark_stable_release_tag_refspec_contract.py`. That file already finds its tests through `globals()`, and it already runs in `ci.yml` (line 1193) and in both release gates' `validate-scripts` jobs. Adding a new test file would also need a sixth path, `ci.yml`, to register it. The complete option (bounded wait plus a fail-closed check of every state, an identical gate script in both workflows, and an accurate notify message when publishing is off) costs well under 30 extra lines compared with a bare check. It adds no dependency and no new external interface, so it is included (Boil the Lake; §6 puts correctness and safety ahead of speed).

## Automation / §20 surface
- No new script and no supervisor. This only changes existing workflow steps and jobs.
- Entry points that change:
  - `.github/workflows/mark-stable.yml` (`workflow_dispatch` on `stable`), `release` job.
  - `.github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml` (`workflow_dispatch`; dispatched by `auto-release-stable.yml` and `promote-main-to-stable.yml`), jobs `release`, `sync-to-main` and `notify`.
- No database work and no `docs/scripts-pending-removal.md` entry.
- Grant: the issue body has no `files_touched` block. If the issue was opened by the pipeline (GH_PAT) login, `scripts/files_touched_scope_guard.py::build_automation_grant` gives it an open grant (`reason=pipeline_author_no_allowlist`). The implementer still edits only these five paths:
  - files_touched:
    - .github/workflows/mark-stable.yml
    - .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml
    - tests/test_mark_stable_release_tag_refspec_contract.py
    - README.md
    - changelog.d/6532-stable-release-ci-lint-gate.md

## 1. Files likely to change
1. `.github/workflows/mark-stable.yml`: `release` job only (around lines 636–1030).
2. `.github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml`: `release` job (around lines 6293–6670), `sync-to-main` (around 6681) and the `notify` status block (around 6966–7000). The file is 395,154 bytes now and will be about 401 KB afterwards, under the 480,000-byte guard (§24). Check with `wc -c` after editing.
3. `tests/test_mark_stable_release_tag_refspec_contract.py`: new `test_*` functions, found automatically by `main()`.
4. `README.md`: two new rows in the Variables table, next to `AUTO_RELEASE_STABLE_ENABLED` / `AUTO_RELEASE_STABLE_MAX_ATTEMPTS` (around line 221).
5. `changelog.d/6532-stable-release-ci-lint-gate.md`: new fragment. Format follows `changelog.d/6839-merge-gate-ci-aggregate-check.md`: a `<!-- changelog: fixed -->` header, then the CLAUDE.md §20 structure.

## 2. Functions / steps to implement (both workflows; step scripts must be byte-identical)

a) Release job `permissions:`. Add a job-level block `contents: write` + `checks: read`. Today only the workflow-level `contents: write` is granted, and without `checks: read` the check-runs read can return 403 on a private repo. Because the gate fails closed, that would block every release. No other scope is added.

b) Release job `env:` (job level), with defaults set in the workflow (§8):
   - `STABLE_RELEASE_ENABLED: ${{ vars.STABLE_RELEASE_ENABLED || 'false' }}`
   - `STABLE_RELEASE_CI_WAIT_SECS: ${{ vars.STABLE_RELEASE_CI_WAIT_SECS || '600' }}`
   - Raise `timeout-minutes` from 10 to 20 so the bounded wait fits.

c) New step `Resolve stable release switch` (`id: release_switch`), placed after "Record the tested commit":
   - Reads the variable only through env and never puts `vars.*` into the script text.
   - Writes `enabled=true` only when the lowercased value is exactly `true`; anything else writes `false`.
   - Logs `STABLE_RELEASE_SWITCH enabled=<true|false>`.

d) New step `Require successful CI lint check-run` (`id: ci_lint_gate`). It goes after "Record the tested commit" and the switch step, and before "Assemble changelog fragments" (the first step that can push). It runs regardless of `dry_run` and of the switch.
   - Env: `GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}`, `CI_CHECK_NAME: lint`.
   - Script outline:
     - `set -euo pipefail`
     - `source scripts/gh_helpers.sh 2>/dev/null || true`, then the standard `gh_retry` fallback line.
     - Fail closed if `RELEASE_TESTED_SHA` does not match `^[0-9a-f]{40}$`.
     - Query `gh_retry gh api "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/commits/${RELEASE_TESTED_SHA}/check-runs?check_name=${CI_CHECK_NAME}&filter=latest&per_page=100"` into a temp file.
   - Classify the response with `jq` (one function):
     - `unreadable`: non-zero exit code, invalid JSON, `.check_runs` not an array, or `total_count` greater than the number of runs returned.
     - Keep only runs where `.name == "lint"` and `.app.slug == "github-actions"`, so a `lint` check-run created by another GitHub App cannot satisfy the gate.
     - `missing`: zero runs left.
     - `incomplete`: any run with `.status != "completed"`.
     - `failed`: any run whose `.conclusion` is not `success` (including cancelled, timed_out, neutral, skipped and stale).
     - `pass`: none of the above.
   - Only `incomplete` is retried: poll every 30 seconds until `STABLE_RELEASE_CI_WAIT_SECS` runs out (an invalid value falls back to 600; `0` means no wait). After that it fails closed as `incomplete`.
   - Every non-pass outcome prints `::error::STABLE_RELEASE_CI_GATE outcome=fail reason=<missing|incomplete|failed|unreadable> sha=<sha> runs=<n>` and exits 1.
   - A pass prints `STABLE_RELEASE_CI_GATE outcome=pass sha=<sha> runs=<n>`.
   - The script must have no `${{ }}` expressions.

e) Step "Assemble changelog fragments": change only its `DRY_RUN` env to `${{ (inputs.dry_run || steps.release_switch.outputs.enabled != 'true') && 'true' || 'false' }}`. When publishing is off, fragments are assembled locally but never committed or pushed (the existing dry-run branch). The script body stays unchanged, so the `RELEASE_TESTED_SHA` assertions in `tests/test_changelog_fragment_contract.py` and `tests/test_apply_analysis_on_main.py` still hold.

f) Steps "Tag version and update stable pointer", "Create GitHub Release" and "Notify consumer repos via repository_dispatch": change only their `if:` to `${{ !inputs.dry_run && steps.release_switch.outputs.enabled == 'true' }}`. Their `run:` bodies stay byte-identical, which the existing `test_workflows_share_identical_publication_logic_and_call_order` requires.

g) New step `Release disabled summary` with `if: ${{ !inputs.dry_run && steps.release_switch.outputs.enabled != 'true' }}`. It prints `::notice::STABLE_RELEASE_DISABLED version=<v> sha=<sha>: validation and the CI lint gate passed; changelog push, tags, GitHub release, consumer dispatch and sync-to-main skipped` and writes a `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` line. The version reaches the script through env.

h) Release job `outputs:` gets `release_enabled: ${{ steps.release_switch.outputs.enabled }}`. Both workflows get it for parity, but only test-and-mark-stable reads it.

i) test-and-mark-stable `sync-to-main` `if:` becomes the existing three conditions plus `&& needs.release.outputs.release_enabled == 'true'`. A missing output means no forward merge. This file is the only one with `sync-to-main`.

j) test-and-mark-stable `notify` status block:
   - Pass `RELEASE_ENABLED: ${{ needs.release.outputs.release_enabled }}` through step env.
   - When `RELEASE=success`, `GATE_ONLY!=true` and `RELEASE_ENABLED!=true`, set `MSG="Release gate <v> PASSED — publishing disabled (STABLE_RELEASE_ENABLED off); nothing tagged"` and `RELEASE_ICON="⊘"`. The success/failure decision itself does not change.

## 3. Data structures affected
- New release-job output `release_enabled` (string `true`/`false`).
- New step outputs `release_switch.enabled`.
- New repo variables `STABLE_RELEASE_ENABLED` (default `false`) and `STABLE_RELEASE_CI_WAIT_SECS` (default `600`).
- New log keys `STABLE_RELEASE_SWITCH`, `STABLE_RELEASE_CI_GATE` and `STABLE_RELEASE_DISABLED`.
- No existing identifier is renamed or removed (§10).

## 4. API / interface changes
- One new GitHub REST read per release run, plus at most `STABLE_RELEASE_CI_WAIT_SECS/30` re-polls, and only while the result is `incomplete`: `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/{ref}/check-runs` with `check_name`, `filter=latest` and `per_page`. With a GitHub token it needs the `checks: read` permission (public REST "List check runs for a Git reference").
- §14 audit: the existing "Verify CI passed" steps call `/commits/{sha}/status`, which is the legacy combined status. GitHub Actions jobs report as check-runs, not statuses, so that call cannot return `lint`. That is why a new call is needed instead of reusing it.
- Behaviour change, as intended: with the variable unset, no release publishes. Operators must set `STABLE_RELEASE_ENABLED=true` to release.

## Decisions
### D1 — Where the CI gate lives
- Chosen: a new step in the `release` job, right after `RELEASE_TESTED_SHA` is recorded and before the changelog push.
- Alternatives considered: (1) Extend the `validate` job's "Verify CI passed" status step. (2) Replace the status call with check-runs.
